paper_title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
core_problem: Traditional reinforcement learning requires extensive weight updates and massive training parameters to improve language agents on complex decision-making and reasoning tasks.
methodology_summary: Reflexion is a novel framework that reinforces language agents through verbal reflection rather than updating weights, using an Actor model for text/action generation, an Evaluator model for scoring outputs, and a Self-Reflection component to update memory via in-context learning.
empirical_results: Achieved 91% pass@1 accuracy on HumanEval, and improved performance over strong baseline approaches by 22% in AlfWorld, 20% in HotPotQA, and 11% on HumanEval.
explicit_limitations: Relies on the LLM's self-evaluation capabilities or heuristics without formal guarantees for optimal success, and depends on environment feedback mechanisms.
